meaning: to work or study late into the night
example: She had to burn the midnight oil to finish the research report before the deadline.
origin: Probably from the time when lamps burned oil, so working late meant using oil at night; the exact origin is uncertain

wrong_meanings.meaning: to waste oil by leaving a lamp on
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This takes the words literally, but the idiom describes working late, not wasting fuel

wrong_meanings.meaning: to start a fire in the middle of the night
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom has nothing to do with fire; it describes working or studying at night

wrong_meanings.meaning: to sleep through the entire night
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is the opposite of the idiom, which describes staying awake to work

explanation: 'Burn the midnight oil' means to work or study late into the night, often to meet a deadline. It is used in everyday speech to describe extra effort outside normal working hours.
